# Insect attraction to light

The data for this activity come from a study which investigates whether insects are more or less attracted to different types of light sources at night. Different types of electric lights emit different wavelengths of light, and it is possible that some may be more attractive to insects, which may disrupt normal insect behavior or cause their death.

The researchers in this study conducted an experiment in which six light traps were set up each night at each of three different locations. Each trap contained a different light source, and the traps were checked the following morning to count the number of insects caught. The experiment was repeated across multiple nights, and the researchers also recorded information about the moon phase, temperature, and humidity each night.

```{r, include=F, eval=F}
bug_data <- read_csv("https://cmustatistics.github.io/data-repository/data/bug-attraction.csv")

bug_data <- bug_data |>
  rename(light_type = `Light Type`,
         moon = `% Moon Visible`,
         mean_temp = `Mean Temp`,
         mean_humid = `Mean Humidity`) |>
  select(Location, light_type, moon, mean_temp, mean_humid,
         Total) |>
  drop_na()

write_csv(bug_data, "~/Documents/Teaching/sta712/sta712-f26.github.io/class_activities/bug_attraction.csv")
```

## Data

The data can be loaded into R with:

```{r message=F, warning=F}
library(tidyverse)

bug_attraction <- read_csv("https://sta712-f26.github.io/class_activities/bug_attraction.csv")
```

The following variables are included:

* `Location`: Location the light trap was placed. `BG` = botanical garden, `LK` = La Kretz field station, `Stunt` = stunt ranch.
* `light_type`: Type of light bulb used to attract insects. `No` means no bulb at all; `A`, `B`, and `C` are all Philips light bulbs whose color can be adjusted by the user; `LED` is a commercial white LED bulb; and `CFL` is a commercial compact fluorescent bulb.
* `moon`: Percentage of moon visible (moon phase).
* `mean_temp`: Mean temperature (Celsius)
* `mean_humid`: Mean humidity (%)
* `Total`: Total number of insects captured in the trap

## Your task

Build a Poisson regression model that will allow you to address the main research question: are some types of light more attractive to insects? Then use model diagnostics to assess whether your model is a good fit to the data.
